## Introduction

How can we do Design Research in One Day??
Let us put together a set of hunches, and find out, [today](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/W22b4e1MtVU?t=23&feature=share), if there is any truth in them. 



## {{< iconify mdi insect size = 1.5em >}} {{< iconify game-icons pointy-hat >}} Free Hunch #1: Guys have more pocket money than Gals.

::: callout-important
{{< iconify academicons hypothesis-square >}} Guys carry more cash than Gals. 
:::

Have you got money? Open your wallet and show me how much. Guys and Gals. 
Will this work in these UPI days? And well-dressed Gals don't have pockets in their clothing, Uncle...

Al right, then ask **"How much did you spend today?"** Again, Guys and Gals. 

And then a two-independent-sample test for means. And Permutation and all that stuff.

## {{< iconify academicons hypothesis-square >}} The average tip people give is higher for people who are non-vegetarians. Regardless of whether you are [going Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Going_Dutch) or not.
:::

Are vegetarians more kanjoos? Or it is the meat-eaters?

So Swiggy/Zomato/Dining Out bills. For both sets of people, and look at the tip amounts. And then ? Which test, peasants?

## {{< iconify mdi insect size = 1.5em >}} {{< iconify game-icons pointy-hat >}} Free Hunch #5: I am an INTJ

::: callout-important
## {{< iconify academicons hypothesis-square >}} Srishti kids are predominantly introverted
:::

What are we looking at, data-wise? A *proportion*, which if more than 50% would justify our hunch. So we do an MBTI <https://www.16personalities.com/free-personality-test> on some unsuspecting **sample** of people, and try to generalize that result to the **population**.


## {{< iconify mdi insect size = 1.5em >}} {{< iconify game-icons pointy-hat >}} Free Hunch #6: Let's Go to ChefsTouch(?)

::: callout-important
## {{< iconify academicons hypothesis-square >}} Most people think the food in the mess/cafeteria is ordinary.
:::
Again, a survey of a sample. Opinions, yes or no. A Proportion for the sample, and an extension to the population. A *proportion test*.

## {{< iconify mdi insect size = 1.5em >}} {{< iconify game-icons pointy-hat >}} Free Hunch #7: Some peasants make, uh, friends earlier. 

::: callout-important
## {{< iconify academicons hypothesis-square >}} People studying Art-related degrees ( B.FA in CAP / DMA / Film ) are more likely to have BF/GFs than other Srishti students studying Design-related degrees ( B.Des / B.Voc / B.Cra ).
:::

Let's say Art people vs Design people. Ask people if they have a BF/GF and since when...And then a prop.test to see if there are differences in proportion.

Make sure you have equal/large nos of all genders in both groups (Art/Design).

## {{< iconify mdi insect size = 1.5em >}} {{< iconify game-icons pointy-hat >}} Free Hunch #8: All Srishti Dads are Weird.

::: callout-important
## {{< iconify academicons hypothesis-square >}} Most Srishti students think their Dad is weird. 
:::

Even if some of them happen to be Girl-Dads. 

So how do we find out? Ask for a "yes/no" opinion from a sample of students. And then a prop.test to see if the proportion is significantly greater than 50%.


## {{< iconify mdi insect size = 1.5em >}} {{< iconify game-icons pointy-hat >}} Free Hunch #9: Which college on campus has more "non-binary" people?

::: callout-important
## {{< iconify academicons hypothesis-square >}} Does the number of people who have non-binary pronouns ( They/Them ) differ significantly between colleges on campus?
:::

So, a survey of people from different colleges on campus, as to what pronouns they use, if any ( He/She/Him/Her, or They/Them). And then a chi-square test to see if there are differences in proportions.

## {{< iconify mdi insect size = 1.5em >}} {{< iconify game-icons pointy-hat >}} Free Hunch #10: Do tattoos make people look attractive or not?

::: callout-important
## {{< iconify academicons hypothesis-square >}} Some peope think tattoos make people look more attractive, while others think the opposite.
:::

So, a survey of people from different colleges on campus, as what their opinion is on tattoos and attractiveness ( Yes / No). Survey Males and Females, Students and Faculty. Check the number of respondents in each sub-group!! And then a chi-square test to see if there are differences in proportions.

## How to Sample a Population?

Here are some simple steps to sample a population (of people)

- Ensure you know how many samples you need ( n = ? )
- Ensure that the population is accessible to you: are the specific category of people numerous and available to you? 
- Method:
  - Walk up to any person whom you have determined to be part of your target population
  - Explain in brief (< 80 seconds) what you are doing, and why you want their help, and in what way
  - Clarify on any data-privacy concerns they may have. **There is no name column in your data.**
  - If they agree to participate:
    - Give them a coin to toss, and you call it
    - If you call correctly, they are part of your sample. If not, not. 
    - Record their responses in your data form. Show them the final recorded response if asked.
    - Either way, pay them.
